notes.text: The central authorial number at the top is 25. Its flanking dark strokes support an enclosing-brace reading, retained with doubt; C’s cancelled 24 cannot be separately recovered. A lighter 58 at the lower left belongs to another unnamed hand and is retained as foliation.

The author introduces p_2 in (37), writes the two equalities joined by the brace of (38), and accompanies them with two diagrams. The words below them are commutatif and est comm. He puts (cart) in the first square and later requires that first square to be cartésien. He also writes that p_1 is transversal p.r. à the immersion bordante b. These are accounts of the manuscript’s assertions, not proof checks.

The author says that p_2 is uniquely determined and invokes the displayed map beginning with the pair (p_1,b) as mono. The cancelled initial b-like component and the surviving comma are preserved. The small sign between the two terminal Sigmas remains <|×, and the shortened map endpoint remains arrow|shaft; no interpretation of these uncertain strokes was used to repair the transcription. The unmatched closing parenthesis in est mono). is retained.

The author replaces suppose by doit and a crossed short word, read tentatively as une, by l’unique. The cancellation hides much of suppose and une, so both remain doubtful. The l’unique insertion attaches after ce qui est, above the crossed word; it does not attach before the b map.

In (39) the author gives x prec y by the displayed existence expression. The small angle is below Sigma in that formula; this explicit placement resolves M0598 to the first reading. The earlier Sigma expressions have raised small angle forms, with the crowded target superscript of (37) still open as angle|star. This is a report of the written positions and symbols; no equivalence of the expressions was assumed or proved.

The dotted source hooks are reproduced with their observed separate components: five in each horizontal hook of the first square, four in the second square, and three in the inline b map. The first square’s right vertical stroke has a rounded filled terminal mark. The curved divider crosses the descender of commutatif without cancelling the word. These graphic readings were based on the visible strokes.
